subject: Money
title: Spain and Ireland 2008
description: A micro-lesson that makes Spain and Ireland 2008 usable.

hook.text: Spain built more houses between 2000 and 2007 than France, Germany, and UK combined. Most were unneeded.

buildup.text: Euro adoption gave Spain and Ireland access to cheap German interest rates. Borrowing exploded.

discovery.text: Construction became Spain's main employer. Ireland's banks lent recklessly. Both economies were hostage to housing.

twist.text: Ireland's bank bailout cost 42% of GDP. Spain's unemployment hit 27%. Youth unemployment exceeded 50%.

climax.text: Joining the euro removed interest rate protection. Countries couldn't adjust monetary policy to local conditions.

punchline.text: Cheap money built too much. Expensive reality followed.

quiz.question: Why did Spain and Ireland experience such severe housing bubbles?
options: Cheap euro-denominated credit fueled excessive building
